note: Item codes are the S1 Data column names with the bracketed value labels stripped (ITEM_RENAME in data/bled_2021_pheno_imagery.py), self-describing (detail/duration/manipulation) and matching S1 Appendix items 1-3 by content. Administered in French (LimeSurvey); item_text is the S1 Appendix French verbatim, item_text_translated is the paper's own English (study_supplied). The appendix prints no separate response options for items 1-3: the alternatives are named inside each stem, so option_text lifts those stem phrases (French) and option_text_translated lifts the paper's English phrases; the actual on-screen button labels are unpublished. instructions = the questionnaire intro plus the block lead-in from S1 Appendix; instructions_translated is this project's translation (machine_translation for that field only). Non-breaking spaces before ':' and '?' normalised to plain spaces. S1 Data header labels pheno_detail as [1=detailed; 2=detailed/blurry; 3=blurry], but the paper (Results s.2) reports 66.7% autistic vs 43.8% control 'detailed', which the data reproduce only at resp=3 (26/39, 35/80); resp=1 gives 7.7%/13.8%. Shipped anchors follow the data: 1=floue/blurry, 2=mixed, 3=detaillee/detailed. The duration (3=persistent: 35.9/20.0) and manipulation (3=always: 56.4/46.3) headers agree with the paper and are shipped as labelled. Raw S1 crosstabs equal the live table cell for cell, so the IRW script did not recode. Instrument is the authors' own 3 items; paper is CC BY 4.0; no rights restriction found.
public_note: For pheno_detail the source data file's header labels 1 as detailed and 3 as blurry, but the paper's reported percentages (66.7% of autistic vs 43.8% of control participants reporting detailed images) match resp = 3 exactly, so this item text labels 3 as detailed and 1 as blurry

source_ref: Bled et al. 2021 PLOS ONE 10.1371/journal.pone.0255039: S1 Appendix (s002.docx, French questionnaire items 5-11); S1 Data (s001.csv headers); Methods section 3 (English items and scoring)
note: Administered in French (online questionnaire, France). item_text/option_text are verbatim from S1 Appendix (pone.0255039.s002.docx, 'Original French version of the questionnaire', items 5-11, leading '5)'..'11)' numbering stripped); item_text_translated is the paper's own English (Methods, 'Use of visual mental representations', 7-item list, PLOS XML italics/line breaks joined). Mapping: data/bled_2021_pheno_imagery.py is a name-preserving rename -- IRW code = S1 Data CSV header with its bracketed value-label suffix stripped (e.g. 'use_recollection [0=words_only; 1=images/words; 2=imges_only]' -> use_recollection); each header names the item's situation (recollection, comprehension, anticipation, planification, problemSolving, decision, memorization), 1:1 with appendix items 5-11 in the same order. resp: header value labels 0=words_only, 1=images/words, 2=imges_only [sic], matching the paper ('words only'=0, 'images and words'=1, 'images only'=2). The French options print as 'Mots / Images / Les deux' (that order), mapped Mots=0, Les deux=1, Images=2; option_text_translated uses the paper's scoring labels, which are glosses rather than literal translations of 'Mots/Images/Les deux'. Deviation: the French stems ask 'des images ou des mots ?' while the paper's English adds 'or both' (the third option is only in the response line); shipped as each source prints it. Instructions left blank: the questionnaire-wide French preamble ('Les questions suivantes portent sur vos experiences internes au quotidien...') has no English in the paper and was not machine-translated; the 'Lorsque vous visualisez...' lead-in belongs to the sibling phenomenology block (items 1-3), not this table. Rights: the study's own purpose-built items (created from prior questionnaires per the paper), published CC BY 4.0 in PLOS ONE; no restriction found. Live counts reproduce the source CSV per item and level 21/21 (verify_bled_2021_imagery_use.R).

source_ref: Nordhoff S, Stapel J, He X, Gentner A, Happee R (2021) PLOS ONE 16(12):e0260953, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0260953 (CC BY 4.0) -- S1 Data workbook pone.0260953.s001: 'Responses' sheet header row for the item codes, 'Descriptive statistics' sheet for the verbatim wording (Q45-Q48), cross-checked against the Table 2 image (.t002); Table 2 caption for the 1-5 anchors
note: Item codes ARE the source column names: data/nordhoff_2021_sae2.py reads the PLOS S1 Data workbook (pone.0260953.s001, 'Responses' sheet) and melts every column matching ^MOTIVE\d+_ with var_name='item', no rename and no positional step (core-model pattern 1; Step 5b exempt on the derivation). The headers embed the item wording in abbreviated form and are carried verbatim, including the source's stray space in 'MOTIVE2_ I_use_my_PAC_...'. WORDS: item_text is the full sentence from the SAME workbook's 'Descriptive statistics' sheet, which lists the motive block as Q45-Q48; these map to MOTIVE1-MOTIVE4 in order, 4/4, each header being the same sentence with 'partly automated car' abbreviated to PAC (safely / comfortably / more pleasurable / other activities unrelated to driving), and all four sentences were checked against the published Table 2 image (.t002). DEVIATION, disclosed: the leading 'Q45. '-style numbering and a trailing space were stripped; nothing else changed. Direction sanity check: the deposited 'Responses' sheet (198 rows; 113-114 non-99 per item, matching live n 114/114/113/114) gives live means comfortably 4.57 > safely 4.36 > pleasurable 4.32 > other activities 2.15, the same rank order as Table 2's full-sample 4.38 > 4.17 > 4.09 > 2.17 (n 612-615) -- the deposit is a subset of the analysed sample, so values differ but order holds. OPTIONS: 1=strongly disagree, 2=disagree, 3=neutral, 4=agree, 5=strongly agree, from the Table 2 caption, which covers these items; the processing script passes values through unchanged except dropping the 99 sentinel, and every item uses all five levels live. instructions/section_prompt blank: the paper only paraphrases the block ('Respondents were further asked for their motives to use their partially automated car') and publishes no verbatim instruction. Administered in English, so no language/_translated columns. No correct_response. Minor source inconsistency, not affecting the text: the workbook gives Q48 SD 1.21 where the printed Table 2 gives 1.15. RIGHTS: the items are the authors' own (Table 2 marks Q47 'Self-created'; Q45, Q46, Q48 cite refs 38, 51 as adapted from the literature), published in a CC BY 4.0 PLOS ONE article and its supplement; not in instrument_rights_register.csv, no test publisher, and no fee, permission, non-commercial, no-derivatives or no-redistribution clause found to quote, so silence is permission. Step 3b: live 4 items x resp 1-5 are exactly the workbook's MOTIVE block, matching the table name; not the TRUST (12) or SAFETY (6) blocks.
